faqs.q: Sec. 78-88. - City seal; signatures remain valid.
faqs.a:
(a)
The clerk may cause the seal of the city to be printed, engraved, stamped, or otherwise
               placed in facsimile on any bond. The facsimile seal has the same legal effect as the
               impression of the seal.
(b)
The bonds and the coupons bearing the signatures of the officers in office at the
               time of the signing thereof shall be the valid and binding obligations of the city,
               notwithstanding that before the delivery thereof and payment therefor, any or all
               of the persons whose signatures appear thereon shall have ceased to fill their respective
               offices.
(c)
Any officer herein authorized or permitted to sign any bond, at the time of its execution
               and of the execution of a signature certificate, may adopt as and for his own facsimile
               signature the facsimile signature of his predecessor in office in the event that such
               facsimile signature appears upon the bond or upon the coupons pertaining thereto or
               upon both the bond and such coupons.
(Code 1981, § 27-89; Ord. No. 551, § 29(K)—(M), 5-14-1964)
